mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the FEDFUNDS rate increased by more than 0.5% within the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points within the last month suggests an improving labor market, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE dropped by more than 0.3 percentage points within the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over the last three months indicates strong consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the periods where RSAFS showed a sustained increase over the last three months.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% within the last month signals a weakening supply side, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic growth slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where INDPRO declined by more than 1% within the last month.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 5% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in the last month, it suggests a strong labor market recovery, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment increase.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 5% and PAYEMS increase > 200k in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE was above 5% and PAYEMS increased by more than 200,000 in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 5% and real GDP (GDPC1) grows by more than 2% in the last quarter, it indicates a strong demand environment, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic activity expands.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increase > 5% and GDPC1 growth > 2% in 1 quarter
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where HOUST increased by more than 5% and GDPC1 grew by more than 2% in the last quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% within the last month signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate tighter monetary policy.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where CPIAUCSL increased by more than 0.5% within the last month.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) and real GDP (GDPC1) both show a decline of more than 1% in the last quarter, it suggests a weakening supply side and overall economic contraction, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings decline.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO and GDPC1 decline > 1% in 1 quarter
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where both INDPRO and GDPC1 declined by more than 1% in the last quarter.
